proposals: Stronger baselines: add a likelihood-ratio detector with the TRUE post-change model (oracle upper bound) and a Kalman-residual chi-square (windowed NIS) test; confirm the candidate is not just matching them.
Alternative detectors: add a kernel / MMD sequential test, an e-process (mixture martingale) detector, and a learned (neural/ensemble) detector trained on simulated failures.
Revised hypothesis: restrict the claim to the regime where the candidate wins (e.g. periodic structural errors, or sparse sampling) and demonstrate it over a finer sparsity grid.
Increase failure realism / difficulty: smaller magnitudes, mixed simultaneous failures, longer ramps; advantages of multi-scale methods usually appear for weak, slowly-developing changes.
Strengthen the diagnostic contribution: report fault-isolation accuracy at EQUAL detection delay, which is often where residual-signature methods separate from CUSUM.
